The mass percentages of the first-named compounds are calculated as follows:

**Sample 1:** Mixture of Ca(OH)₂ and MgCO₃ (initial mass 24.48 g, residue 12.93 g, loss 11.55 g).  
Let \(n_1\) and \(n_2\) be moles of Ca(OH)₂ and MgCO₃.  
Masses: \(74.092n_1 + 84.313n_2 = 24.48\)  
Losses: \(18.015n_1 + 44.009n_2 = 11.55\)  
Solving gives \(n_1 = 0.0594352\), so mass Ca(OH)₂ = \(74.092 \times 0.0594352 = 4.40367\) g.  
Percentage = \((4.40367 / 24.48) \times 100 = 17.9889\% \rightarrow 18.0\%\).

**Sample 2:** Mixture of ZnCO₃ and NaCl (initial 14.51 g, residue 11.51 g, loss 3.00 g).  
Only ZnCO₃ decomposes: loss = \(44.009/125.388\) per gram.  
Mass ZnCO₃ = \(3.00 \times 125.388/44.009 = 8.54743\) g.  
Percentage = \((8.54743 / 14.51) \times 100 = 58.907\% \rightarrow 58.9\%\).

**Sample 3:** Mixture of K₂CO₃ and MgCO₃ (initial 17.03 g, residue 13.03 g, loss 4.00 g).  
Only MgCO₃ decomposes: loss = \(44.009/84.313\) per gram.  
Mass MgCO₃ = \(4.00 \times 84.313/44.009 = 7.66325\) g, so mass K₂CO₃ = \(17.03 - 7.66325 = 9.36675\) g.  
Percentage = \((9.36675 / 17.03) \times 100 = 55.001\% \rightarrow 55.0\%\).

Thus the three percentages are 18.0, 58.9, 55.0.

ANSWER: 18.0,58.9,55.0
